And although everything in this island was at one's beck and call, a single thing was nevertheless lacking. **Water** was not to be had, except with great difficulty. There were indeed many who attempted, in part, to bring the **Water of a Spring** <note>original: *Aqua Fontis*</note> there through channels; others also tried to extract it from various things. But their attempted labor was in vain, because it could be obtained in those places by no such means. And if it was obtained, it was nevertheless useless and poisonous, unless it was drawn from the rays of the **Sun** or the **Moon** <note>original: *Solis vel Lunae*</note>, which few were able to accomplish. Even he who had fortune favor him in perfecting this could never attract more than ten parts. For this **Water** was of a wonderful sort; and believe me, for I have seen with my own eyes and touched the snowy whiteness of that **Water**. While I was contemplating that water, I was greatly changed. Meanwhile, exhausted by that consideration, **Neptune** vanished from before my eyes, and there appeared to me a great man, upon whose forehead the name of **Saturn** was inscribed. <summary>The narrator describes the rare celestial water required for the alchemical trees, which can only be gathered from the rays of the Sun and Moon, before Neptune is replaced by a figure named Saturn.</summary>
